title: Multi-Cloud DNS Resolution Latency

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.4.20 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.4.20 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=cloud` sourcetype=`dns:resolution` collected via Custom scripted input (dig, nslookup); validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=cloud sourcetype="dns:resolution"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress

| sort -_time
description: Cross-provider DNS query performance comparison. Slow or failed resolution causes application timeouts and user experience degradation.
value: Detecting multi-cloud dns resolution latency early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Run periodic DNS probes (dig, nslookup, or custom script) from Lambda, Azure Functions, Cloud Functions, or on-prem agents. Measure resolution time per domain. Ingest results via HEC with fields: provider, vantage_point, domain, resolution_ms, success. Alert when avg latency exceeds 200ms or failure rate > 5%. Compare providers for DNS migration decisions.
visualization: Line chart (resolution latency by provider and domain over time), Table (provider, domain, avg ms), Heat map (provider vs domain).
knownFalsePositives: This pattern can surge during change windows, in sandboxes, and when a platform is in maintenance, so we line alerts up with the calendar and take a second look before we call it an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=cloud`.
• Install and configure Custom scripted input (dig, nslookup) with the modular input for `dns:resolution`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.4.33.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Run periodic DNS probes (dig, nslookup, or custom script) from Lambda, Azure Functions, Cloud Functions, or on-prem agents. Measure resolution time per domain. Ingest results via HEC with fields: provider, vantage_point, domain, resolution_ms, success. Alert when avg latency exceeds 200ms or failure rate > 5%. Compare providers for DNS migration decisions.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="dns:resolution" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="dns:resolution"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.20_multi_cloud_dns_resoluti_20"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `dns:resolution` in `index=cloud` to detect multi-cloud dns resolution latency. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_20_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (resolution latency by provider and domain over time), Table (provider, domain, avg ms), Heat map (provider vs domain)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Custom scripted input (dig, nslookup) and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of multi-cloud dns resolution latency so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
